ie-0oal.title: Landscape: mountains with no coast in view
ie-0oal.summary: The Wicklow Mountains, south of the capital, look like the western coastal mountains. You never see the coast from them, and small roads here have Gen 4 rather than the older Gen 2 typical of the west.

ie-2Zr0.title: Landscape: rugged wild hills, moors in the west
ie-2Zr0.summary: The west coast has steep hills and low mountains, wild moorland and grass in brown and yellow tones, with sometimes bare rock. The neat fields of the east give way.

ie-5CWT.title: Road lines: yellow dashes on the edge
ie-5CWT.summary: Yellow dashed lines along the road edge are very common. The UK almost never has them. New Zealand has them too.

differs.how: UK roads almost never have yellow edge dashes

ie-5rT8.title: Phone numbers: two-digit area code
ie-5rT8.summary: Numbers start with a two-digit area code grouped by region by its first digit, so it is easy to learn.

ie-616V.title: Pole: wooden with metal crossbars
ie-616V.summary: Wooden poles sometimes have metal crossbars. The UK has them too, and so do Sweden and Finland.

ie-7jug.title: Language: Irish in italics under English
ie-7jug.summary: Signs are often bilingual: English in regular letters and Irish in italics, with place names and phrases translated. Less common on non-official signs.

ie-8zJQ.title: Landscape: green fields with hedgerows
ie-8zJQ.summary: Very green farmland with lots of hedgerows beside roads and between fields. Also common in much of the UK and can look the same.

ie-Avrb.title: Sign: yellow diamond warning signs
ie-Avrb.summary: The only European country with yellow diamond-shaped warning signs. Regulatory signs have the normal red border and white background.

ie-FO2a.title: Bollard: green and white
ie-FO2a.summary: Green and white bollards, not entirely unique but very helpful in 50-50s with the UK.

differs.how: UK bollards are not usually green and white

ie-Gvq4.title: Road: tiny lane with grass strip
ie-Gvq4.summary: Tiny rural roads (boreens) often have a strip of grass in the middle. Not unique, but a strong clue in a tough 50-50 with the UK.

ie-Iiqc.title: Houses: cream walls, black roofs
ie-Iiqc.summary: Cream-white houses with black roofs, sometimes with grey corner stones. Cities have rows of terraces. British-style brick buildings still exist here too.

ie-Kiq5.title: Pole: wooden with metal step rods
ie-Kiq5.summary: Wooden utility poles, often with thin horizontal metal rods bolted on as steps. The UK has the same.

ie-N93o.title: Route marker: 3-digit regional road numbers
ie-N93o.summary: The first digit of a 3-digit regional road number tells you the part of the country. Numbers go anti-clockwise around the island, starting at the capital. Numbers starting with 8 or 9 are newer and not tied to a region.

ie-Ottv.title: Road lines: double yellow at the edge
ie-Ottv.summary: In and near towns, double yellow lines at the road edge mean no parking. Also common in the UK. Nowhere else in Europe except Malta.

ie-R9jd.title: Landscape: hilly big city
ie-R9jd.summary: Cork is much hillier than the other big Irish cities.

ie-SSZH.title: Google car: grey back with black semicircle
ie-SSZH.summary: An electric car with a Gen 4 camera covered most of the east and parts of the northwest. Its back is visible: grey with a black semicircle. Some Gen 4 near the capital still uses the regular blue car.

ie-VCo7.title: Google car: low camera, big round blur
ie-VCo7.summary: Gen 4 camera mounted lower than usual, with a big round blur and a small bump at the front. The blur can be see-through, which makes it easy to miss.

ie-Wp2T.title: Driving side: left
ie-Wp2T.summary: Traffic drives on the left, as in the UK. Malta and Cyprus also do, but the landscape tells them apart.

ie-Xamt.title: Sign: give way sign says YIELD
ie-Xamt.summary: Give-way signs say YIELD. UK ones say GIVE WAY.

ie-Y78L.title: Landscape: bare grey limestone
ie-Y78L.summary: Around Burren National Park, bare grey limestone rock covers the land in a unique karst landscape.

ie-k4AI.title: Landscape: flat-topped mountains
ie-k4AI.summary: In the north of Sligo and Leitrim, mountains have flat, table-like tops.

ie-koXg.title: Sign: black-white post with yellow ball
ie-koXg.summary: Pedestrian crossings are often marked by a black-and-white post with a yellow bulb on top rather than a sign. The UK uses exactly the same posts.

ie-liz2.title: Pole: yellow sticker, lightning bolt only
ie-liz2.summary: Yellow warning stickers on utility poles. Irish ones have a lightning bolt but no person being zapped, and often a second black-outlined sticker below it. UK stickers show a person being zapped.

differs.how: UK stickers show a person being zapped

ie-lm-474349.title: Pole: wooden pole with slanted top
ie-lm-474349.summary: France, Ireland and the UK can be hard to tell apart. Look at the tops of wooden poles: Irish ones are slanted.

differs.how: French pole tops are not slanted
UK pole tops are not slanted

ie-lm-515552.title: Guardrail: A and B types, no reflectors
ie-lm-515552.summary: Both A-type and B-type guardrails with no reflectors, like Germany. The UK only uses A-type.

ie-lm-740286.title: Sign: blue street sign with district number
ie-lm-740286.summary: Blue street signs with white text, a white border and a number on the right showing the postal district.

ie-q0Q1.title: Chevron: yellow on black
ie-q0Q1.summary: Yellow arrows on a black background, with single or multiple arrows. UK chevrons are white on black.

differs.how: UK chevrons are white on black

ie-rRE9.title: Plate: long white, blue strip on left
ie-rRE9.summary: Long white plates with the European blue strip on the left. The white back plate is the key difference from the UK, which has yellow back plates and often no blue strip.

differs.how: UK back plates are yellow, usually no blue strip

ie-wBpf.title: Farm gate: rounded corners
ie-wBpf.summary: Rural metal gates with rounded corners are very common. UK gates usually have square corners, but Northern Ireland also has rounded ones.

differs.how: UK gates usually have square corners

ie-wmsQ.title: Coverage: hilly tiny lane in Gen 4
ie-wmsQ.summary: A very small, thin road with no lines, sometimes with grass in the middle, in hilly land and Gen 4 coverage, probably means Donegal in the northwest. Not exclusive to it.
